clue.text: President is no longer hard in government, not facing uprising

parts.note: something that is no longer simply was
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
G is a standard abbreviation for government, as in G-man

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising up means the word not is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A political commentator notes that a leader is no longer taking a tough line in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing uprising' turns NOT into TON, which closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States.

clue.text: Opening success involving American and America

indicators.note: the word for success wraps around, so involves, the letter for American

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a hit record
US, the United States, stands for America

explanation.surface: An opening night proves a hit with American audiences and America in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or break, an opening in something continuous.

clue.text: Discussion expected to secure one a diary

parts.note: something due is expected, like a baby due next month

a log is a daily record, a diary

explanation.surface: A discussion is planned to obtain a diary for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation or exchange of views, a discussion.

clue.text: Youngsters following band reduced source of ringing in ears?

explanation.surface: Young fans trail a band whose noisy set leaves their ears ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a church tower's bells ringing out, heard by everyone's ears nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A belfry is the tower or chamber housing church bells, so it is where the ringing comes from.

clue.text: I'm going to Barnet, not losing love dwelling within

parts.note: taken as written, without its apostrophe

indicators.note: the word not drops one of its letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone announces a trip to Barnet, a district of north London, without losing their love.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanent describes something inherent, existing or remaining within.

clue.text: US writer's version of Bible including disciple but overlooking name

indicators.note: the Bible version holds the shortened disciple inside it

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: the disciple's name leaves out one letter

parts.note: Simon Peter was one of the twelve disciples

explanation.surface: An American author's take on scripture features a disciple but skips over a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was an American author famous for his science fiction.

clue.text: Point is remade, retaining good pointer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the letter for good held inside them
the letters of the words point and is are made afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A point is reworked while keeping a good indicator of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remade' rearranges POINT IS round G ('retaining good'), but the answer needs a second S where the printed words give a second I, a slip in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost points the way, so it is a pointer.

clue.text: Employs charges after account goes missing

indicators.note: the letters for account disappear from the word for charges

parts.note: to accuse someone is to charge them with an offence

explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to employ it; both verbs are third person.

clue.text: Foolish crime in U.S. state not initiated

a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime in moral terms

explanation.surface: A daft offence is committed in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid, like an ass, so foolish.

clue.text: Wall decorations, say, excellent hint of culture, though covered in plant growth

indicators.note: the excellent and the hint sit inside the plant growth, covered by it

parts.note: moss is a small plant that grows over stones and walls

indicators.note: only the first letter of culture is used

explanation.surface: Fine wall art with a touch of culture lies hidden under moss.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosaics are pictures made of small tiles, often on walls, so they are examples of wall decorations.

clue.text: House, rented out, done over as inn

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for rented out runs backwards

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A rented house has been renovated as a pub.

clue.text: Fellow totters beside the way, tumbling over bits and pieces

parts.note: a totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man, who collects junk; ragmen is another name for them

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A man staggers along the roadside before falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totters' looks like a verb of staggering; it is the British noun for rag-and-bone men, door-to-door scrap collectors.

clue.text: No influence about — for instance — flowers

indicators.note: the word for influence goes round the example abbreviation

parts.note: having a say is having influence
EG, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: Flowers, for example, have no power at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers, a posy.

clue.text: Resentful former priest dismissed about note

indicators.note: the shortened word for former goes round the note
the letters for priest are sent away from the word for former

parts.note: previous means former, earlier

explanation.surface: A bitter ex-priest is removed from post over a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Being envious means feeling jealous of another's luck, so resentful.

clue.text: Chuck blade here?

parts.note: chuck and blade are cuts of beef, so a knife for cutting them; the surface suggests throwing a blade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a verb meaning throw, but chuck and blade are both cuts of beef, which the knife slices.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife with a serrated edge for cutting cooked cuts of beef at the table.

clue.text: Drink most of quantity of salty water

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: a tear is a drop of salty water from the eye

explanation.surface: Someone drinks nearly all of a measure of brine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot beverage, a drink brewed from leaves.

clue.text: Corporation investing in gold, note, almost entirely heading for fall?

indicators.note: the stomach puts itself into gold, so it comes right after it

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
corporation is old slang for a paunch, a tum

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for entirely is dropped

parts.note: all means wholly, entirely

explanation.surface: A company putting money into gold is almost certainly heading for a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is old British slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American word for autumn, so something autumnal is of the season when leaves fall.

clue.text: Much of urban demand falls back, affected by price changes

indicators.note: the pieces drop back and are read in reverse order
the final letter is dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: a city is the urban setting
sales measure demand for goods

explanation.surface: Consumer demand in towns drops away as prices shift.
explanation.definitionFit: In economics, demand is elastic when it responds strongly to changes in price.

clue.text: Agreement about ringing up to get self-assembly accessory

indicators.note: in a down clue, the whole assembly is read upwards
the assent goes round the ringing

parts.note: yea is a word of assent, agreement
a knell is the ringing of a bell

explanation.definitionFit: An Allen key is a small hexagonal wrench supplied with flat-pack furniture to put it together.

clue.text: Memory in stick identifying vitamin source

indicators.note: the memory piece goes inside the stick

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
learning by rote is learning from memory

explanation.surface: A memory stick is found carrying evidence of a vitamin.

clue.text: Lug (as in hearing) or another part of the body?

indicators.note: the word for lug is heard, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to lug is to haul, to tow

explanation.surface: An ear, which hears, or some other body part?
explanation.walkthrough: Lug is also British slang for ear, so 'another part of the body' plays on that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The toe is a digit of the foot, a different body part from the ear.

clue.text: No decision yet in girl's sport

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

clue.text: Result of blaze: contents of mine on the beach

parts.note: ash is what a fire leaves
ore is what a mine yields

explanation.surface: A fire's aftermath and a mine's yield turn up on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land beside the sea, so on the beach.

clue.text: Carefully identify each marine vessel in flood

parts.note: RM, Royal Marines, stands for a marine
Noah's ark was the vessel in the Flood

explanation.surface: Each sailor must pick out a boat when the waters rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to mark out or set aside something for a purpose, to single it out.

clue.text: Impound all but first of coins, seizing silver

indicators.note: the shortened coins hold the silver tight inside
the first letter of the word for coins is dropped

parts.note: pence are British coins
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Seize almost all the coins, grabbing the silver too.
explanation.definitionFit: To encage is to shut up in a cage, and to impound is to shut up in a pound or enclosure.

clue.text: MMORPG character, a sailor following senior naval officer

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the officer

parts.note: VA is short for Vice Admiral
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: In an online role-playing game, a sailor tags along behind an admiral.

clue.text: Recalled my special arrangement of Chopin for orchestra?

the letters of Chopin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remembers their own special orchestration of a Chopin piano work.

clue.text: Residential consequence of endless economic failure?

indicators.note: the word for economic failure loses its last letter

parts.note: a slump is a sharp economic downturn

clue.text: Hint of weakness one found in metal brace

indicators.note: the hint and the one sit inside the metal

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

clue.text: Possibly on plane in trouble

an idiom for being stuck in a difficult position

explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft; it is the plane tree.

clue.text: Wizard twisted genetic material in flower
